name: Mehul Colours Limited
summary: Unranked watchlist pending reporting and execution evidence. Genuine masterbatch manufacturing and profitable legacy operations, but recent margin compression, weak adjusted cash conversion and unproven incremental returns. G2 and G4 are Hold-unresolved. Descriptive BQS4.9 and GQS5.2 do not confer ranking eligibility; IAS is NS.

gates.reason: No proven severe minority abuse. Ownership, no pledge and lower remuneration are positives, while ICD terms, approvals, relatedness and financial-statement corrections need clarification.

Full statutory report reviewed. CARO contradicts audited IPO and investment/loan activity; other reporting inconsistencies also require signed correction. The clean main and IFC opinions do not resolve these facts. This is an unresolved reliability hold, not a proven fraud or automatic failure.

Base funding is adequate after earmarks, treasury haircuts and obligations. Linked downside requires explicit rescue; verify current project certification, restrictions, treasury realizations and collections.
The 1,600-share lot is verified, but the cutoff executable quote,20/60-session trading capacity and zero-turnover days are not. No claim of untradeability or structural failure is made.

material_facts: Promoter and group ownership is 71.65%; no pledge is disclosed and remuneration declined year-on-year.
Unsecured ICD principal of ₹3 crore, financial investments and substantial family rent create capital-allocation and related-party oversight questions.
GOV.contrary_fact_or_search: The main audit is unmodified and fraud is not reported. Specific audit contradictions are assessed in G 2, rather than described as proven misconduct.
GOV.reasoning: Mixed stewardship: no established abuse, but non-operating credit exposure and disclosure corrections limit confidence.

material_facts: Color matching, dispersion know-how, laboratories and an operating history support useful customer relationships.
Top 10 customers represent 48.19% of sales; purchase-order demand and replicable compounding constrain switching-cost claims.
MOAT.contrary_fact_or_search: The masterbatch mix was 84.17% in FY2025 and legacy margins exceed broader peers, but customer retention and qualification data do not establish durable pricing power.
MOAT.reasoning: A useful technical process is not yet a demonstrated structural competitive advantage.

material_facts: Visually verified FY2021 operating revenue₹15.024685crore gives a five-year CAGR of15.14% throughFY2026. The preferred five-year schedule starts7; no acquisition or structural perimeter change is disclosed.
FY2023–26 CAGR is12.81%, FY2023–25 production CAGR2.49%, and FY2026 value-added growth only2.49% despite sales growth33.22%.
REV.contrary_fact_or_search: The older FY2021 comparative is not separately restated, and the FY2022 original/reclassified revenue difference is0.16%. No guaranteed pass-through formula exists; this is comparable nominal revenue growth, not proof of identical physical-volume growth.
REV.reasoning: Use the now-established preferred five-year window, rather than treating it as missing or selecting the best-looking window. Starting7, maximum net negative adjustment1 for current raw-material/mix distortion gives REV6. Retain three-year and physical/value-added cross-checks. No extra low-base penalty or alternate sector rubric.

material_facts: Packaging, consumer and engineering-plastic uses provide genuine repeat demand.
Combined capacity can rise to 2.16 millionkg, but old plants were 86.37% utilized and expansion timing/customer access need verification.
DUR.contrary_fact_or_search: Recycling/substitution pressures and customer concentration temper a large headline plastic-market opportunity.
DUR.reasoning: There is an accessible runway, with material execution and demand constraints.

material_facts: Adjusted three-year incremental ROIC is 10.40%, below the assumed 12–15% cost-of-capital range.
FY2026 average productive-capital ROIC is 32.82%, reflecting profitable legacy operations rather than proven new-plant returns.
CAP.contrary_fact_or_search: Earmarked IPO cash and treasury assets are excluded from productive capital so idle proceeds are not unfairly penalized.
CAP.reasoning: Mixed additional-capital economics; a meaningful aggregate incremental ratio is available, so missing private cohorts do not force NS.

material_facts: FY2024–26 analytically adjusted CFO/PAT is 48.26%, after correcting capital advances and investment gains.
Net receivables outgrew FY2026 sales and closing DSO rose to 95.54 days.
CASH.contrary_fact_or_search: Doubtful receivables are fully provided and the proportion of good balances older than six months improved. Capital advances are not counted again as poor conversion.
CASH.reasoning: Persistently weak realization of profits and greater collection funding needs, not an inability to generate accounting profit.

material_facts: Bank cash and financial investments can fund the modeled base project after preserving IPO earmarks.
Linked downside stress breaches the operating cash floor and needs explicit rescue funding.
BAL.contrary_fact_or_search: Total borrowings are only ₹1.9617 crore, with no reported bank repayment default. No ICD collections are assumed for funding.
BAL.reasoning: Manageable base obligations, with meaningful collections, project-cost and treasury-realization sensitivities.

material_facts: Existing production rose modestly and FY2025 utilization of 86.37% demonstrates operating delivery.
The original March 2026 commissioning target is not verified complete; only 25.43% of the IPO capex allocation was used by 31 March 2026.
EXEC.contrary_fact_or_search: Low IPO utilization does not itself prove abandonment or exclude separately funded internal spending. Existing plants continued to grow sales.
EXEC.reasoning: Mixed delivery evidence and one important unverified project milestone, not an assumed history of repeated failure.

material_facts: FY2026 operating EBITDA fell 12.50% while other income rose 58.09%.
Current-issued-share EPS is ₹4.95,32.18% below FY2025 ₹7.30; other income is 20.02% of PBT.
EARN.contrary_fact_or_search: FY2022–25 profits improved strongly without acquisition. Removing all other income is conservative because some FX and packing income may be operating-like.
EARN.reasoning: The latest nominal sales acceleration has not translated into recurring per-share profit growth.

sections.title: Identity, mandate and information boundary
sections.text:
Mehul Colours Limited is the polymer colour/masterbatch manufacturer on BSE SME, code 544472 and symbol MEHUL, ISIN INE1KH601014. It is not Mehul Telecom. Incorporated on 12 December 1995, it converted to public status on 16 December 2024 and adopted its current name on 9 January 2025. The listed CIN is L25209MH1995PLC095225; stale report headers retaining the unlisted prefix U are a documentary inconsistency, not another company.

The financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards: no subsidiary, associate or joint venture is disclosed. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026. Reports were retrieved on 22 October, but later economic events are excluded. FY2026 is the latest complete audited year; FY2027 H1 was not found published by the cutoff. Fiscal years end 31 March; financial figures below are ₹crore unless stated otherwise.

sections.title: Conclusion and gates before valuation
sections.text:
Conclusion: an unranked watchlist candidate requiring specific reporting and execution evidence, not a demonstrated growth compounder. G1 is Conditional, G2 Hold-unresolved, G3 Conditional and G4 Hold-unresolved. Genuine manufacturing, high legacy margins and modest debt are positive. Against them sit margin compression, weak adjusted cash conversion, below-hurdle incremental returns and an unverified capacity milestone.

The complete statutory report contains CARO statements contradicted by audited IPO and financial-investment/loan notes. A clean main audit and IFC opinion do not resolve that inconsistency. Signed clarification is necessary; this is not an accusation of fraud. Descriptive BQS 4.9 and GQS 5.2 are calculated from exact unrounded 4.90 and 5.15, but G2 excludes both from quality rankings. IAS is NS because the authenticated entry quote and execution evidence are absent. A favorable conditional model cannot override these gates.

sections.title: Actual business and unit economics
sections.text:
This is genuine masterbatch manufacturing rather than merely a chemical trader. The prospectus describes resin selection, pigment/additive formulation, mixing, extrusion, pelletizing and quality control at two Vasai units. FY2025 masterbatch sales were ₹19.2083 crore,84.17% of revenue; pigments were ₹3.6137 crore,15.83%. Separate pigment make/buy/trading margins are not disclosed, so it would be wrong to claim every pigment sale was manufactured in-house.

Raw materials include polymer carriers such as PP, PE, EVA, PET, LDPE and LLDPE, plus TiO2, carbon black and other pigments. Customer-specific color matching and dispersion know-how are useful, but do not alone establish patented technology, contractual switching barriers or persistent pricing power. Selling prices and raw-material costs affect the conversion spread. FY2026 material cost rose to 57.56% of sales from 45.70%; this is central to the profit bridge, not just an incidental cost variance. All other income is removed in the core operating model, conservatively excluding some potentially operating FX/packing income too.

sections.title: Market, moat and customer concentration
sections.text:
Demand comes from packaging, consumer products and engineering plastics, with repeat applications but no guaranteed market-share gains. A large global plastics market is not sufficient evidence of Mehul’s accessible opportunity. Top 10 customer concentration improved from 56.38% in FY2023 to 48.19% in FY2025; top 3 still contributed 26.64% and top 5 34.85%. Orders are substantially purchase-order driven, without disclosed long-term volume guarantees.

Top 10 suppliers represented 65.76% of FY2025 purchases and top 3 40.30%. The risk disclosure says raw-material increases may not be recovered from customers; it does not describe a mechanically guaranteed pass-through contract. Reliable color matching, consistent dispersion and service can retain accounts, but no customer cohort, retention rate or quantified qualification period demonstrates strong switching costs. High margins versus broader peers are a contrary positive, though mix, size and FY2025 peak spreads can explain them without a structural moat. MOAT 4 reflects useful but contestable capability.

sections.title: Growth decomposition and comparable basis
sections.text:
A visually verified FY2021 statutory comparative supplies operating revenue₹15.024685 crore, not total income₹15.131216 crore. Revenue reaches₹30.4032 crore inFY2026, giving a five-year comparable nominal CAGR 15.14%. Following the framework preference, this is the scoring window. The FY2021 base is not separately restated; the known FY2022 original revenue₹20.292484 crore versus later restated₹20.2606 crore difference is only₹.031884 crore,0.16%, largely revenue/other-income classification. No acquisition or structural perimeter change is disclosed. Exact organic physical growth is not claimed.

The shorter FY2023–26 nominal CAGR 12.81% and FY2022–26 four-year CAGR 10.68% remain cross-checks. Actual production FY2023/24/25 was 1,055,856/1,089,903/1,109,039 kg, a two-year CAGR 2.49%, versus same-period nominal revenue CAGR 3.81%. FY2026 sales then grew 33.22%, but value added after materials and inventory change grew only 2.49%, and operating EBITDA declined. A FY2026 physical-volume/product-mix bridge is missing. Three-year value-added CAGR 9.60% is a cross-check, not a replacement scoring rubric.

REV starts 7 for the preferred five-year revenue CAGR and receives the maximum net negative adjustment of one point for the demonstrated current raw-material/mix distortion, ending 6. There is no separate repeated low-base penalty, no favorable trajectory adjustment and no guaranteed commodity pass-through contract inferred. H1 FY2026 revenue₹14.2140 crore and derived H2₹16.1892 crore confirm nominal growth, while H2 PAT falls to₹1.93 crore. This is real reported scale with uncertain underlying physical acceleration, not a clean high-growth volume story.

sections.title: Historical finances and per-share earnings
sections.text:
The historical schedule includes sales, cost categories, PBT, PAT, CFO, net cash capex, cash, equity, borrowings, PPE, financial investments, receivables, inventory and payables. Later restated statements take precedence over older filings; FY2022 is sourced from the DRHP because the final prospectus begins with FY2023. Prior-year presentation differences are not silently mixed.

FY2026 sales were ₹30.4032 crore, PBT ₹7.0348 crore and PAT ₹5.2229 crore. Subtract all ₹1.4084 crore other income: core EBIT is ₹5.6457 crore and EBITDA ₹6.0297 crore, down 12.50% from ₹6.8909 crore. Other income includes investment interest ₹.5232 crore, ICD interest ₹.0927 crore, investment gains ₹.3575 crore, vehicle-sale gains ₹.1059 crore and FX gains ₹.1648 crore. Do not capitalize those earnings and also add their underlying assets at full value.

Reported EPS ₹5.49 sits beside a 10,549,040-share denominator that mathematically gives ₹4.95. A properly time-weighted IPO share count could explain ₹5.49, but the label needs correction. Current-share earning power is ₹4.9511,32.18% below FY2025 ₹7.30, while PAT fell 5.09%. The 25:1 bonus altered units but not ownership wealth; the fresh IPO expanded shares 39.89% and diluted old-holder ownership 28.51%. EARN 4 reflects the latest operating and per-share deterioration, while recognizing strong earlier profit growth.

sections.title: Cash conversion and working capital
sections.text:
Reported FY2026 CFO of ₹.1893 crore requires two adjustments. Add back ₹2.2076 crore capital advances classified within operating cash, then remove ₹.3575 crore financial-investment gains retained there in the annual report. Analytical operating CFO is ₹2.0394 crore. Economic cash capex is ₹2.2009 crore net fixed-asset purchases plus ₹2.2076 crore advances, or ₹4.4085 crore; normalized manufacturing FCF is therefore −₹2.3691 crore.

FY2025 adjusted CFO ₹2.5980 crore less economic capex ₹1.6762 crore gives ₹.9218 crore FCF. FY2024–26 adjusted CFO/PAT is 48.26%. FY2023’s unusually strong CFO benefited from a ₹2.9077 crore receivable release, which is not recurring margin. The published FY2026 cash bridge reconciles opening ₹1.2930 crore plus CFO.1893, investing −8.0788 and financing 20.9269 to closing 14.3305, within ₹.0001 crore rounding.

FY2026 net receivables rose 43.40% to ₹7.958 crore while sales rose 33.22%; closing DSO increased from 88.76 to 95.54 days. However, good balances older than six months fell proportionally from 4.98% to 3.95%, and doubtful ₹.2918 crore is fully provided. Inventory rose 12.36% to ₹2.3385 crore, below sales growth. No factoring/disguised-collection evidence was found. CASH 4 reflects adjusted conversion and collection funding, not a double penalty for project capex.

sections.title: Governance and full statutory audit review
sections.text:
The main independent report, IFC Annexure A and CARO Annexure B were reviewed in full. Main/IFC opinions are unmodified; the auditor states audit-trail controls operated, and reports no fraud, bank repayment default or auditor resignation. Those are real positives, not a substitute for checking annexures.

CARO clauses 3/4 state that no investment/loan activity occurred during FY2026, despite notes showing ₹9.4725 crore MF/PMS assets and ₹3 crore ICD principal. Clause 10(a) says no IPO, despite the ₹21.6576 crore issue and the same auditor’s proceeds-use certificate. Clause 14’s internal-audit applicability statement conflicts with the Board’s internal-auditor appointment/review disclosure. These specific contradictions justify G2 Hold pending signed correction and scope explanation; fraud is not established.

Other issues include the EPS denominator label, a gratuity closing footnote of 14.21 lakhs versus aggregate provision 55.01 lakhs, and stale CIN headers. The May results versus annual CFO/CFI difference of ₹.3575 crore is an investment-gain classification change with unchanged cash, not independently proof of missing cash. The receivables note also says management’s promoter/group list was relied on without independently determining completeness.

At 30 September 2026 promoter/group ownership was 71.65%, with no disclosed pledge. FY2026 promoter-director remuneration ₹.65 crore and family rent ₹.624 crore total 24.39% of PAT; remuneration fell from ₹1.15 crore. Material related-party economics warrant scrutiny, not automatic abuse claims. Obtain ICD terms, maturity, relatedness, approvals and recoverability. Disclosed TDS arrears ₹1.97 lakh and disputed GST ₹4.13 lakh are small statutory matters, not bank defaults.

sections.title: Incremental returns and capital allocation
sections.text:
Productive capital is defined consistently as equity plus interest-bearing debt, less bank cash, MF/PMS assets and ICD principal. It retains PPE, working capital and capital advances. That capital rises from ₹4.2094 crore in FY2023 to ₹16.4266 crore in FY2026. Operating NOPAT at a constant 25% tax assumption rises from ₹2.96415 crore to ₹4.234275 crore.

Three-year incremental ROIC is ₹1.270125 crore/₹12.2172 crore=10.40%, below an explicitly assumed 12–15% cost-of-capital range. The denominator is positive and economically material, so this is not an NM ratio requiring an invented cohort substitute. Project timing and year-end working capital influence it. In contrast, FY2026 NOPAT on average FY2025–26 productive capital is 32.82%, showing strong legacy profitability but not proof of new-plant returns.

Removing IPO cash avoids penalizing idle funding as if already invested in operations. Removing financial investments avoids attributing treasury yield to manufacturing. CAP 5 represents mixed incremental economics rather than a blanket verdict on the profitable legacy business. The future model separately finances working-capital growth, maintenance and project spending; headline ROCE cannot replace that funding bridge.

Capital reconciliation: cumulative FY2024–26 net cash PPE spending ₹3.7633 crore plus capital-advance increases ₹2.8972 crore gives ₹6.6605 crore economic cash capex. Less depreciation ₹1.0532 crore and plus ₹.3124 crore disposal/exchange/noncash residual gives ₹5.9197 crore growth in net PPE plus capital advances. Net trade working capital (receivables+inventory −payables) increases ₹6.0670 crore, from ₹3.6616 crore to ₹9.7286 crore. Other net operating assets/liabilities contribute the residual ₹.2305 crore. Total ₹5.9197+6.0670+.2305=₹12.2172 crore. The two explicit residuals sum ₹.5429 crore,4.44% of the capital increase; the detailed disposal/tax/provision allocation remains uncertain rather than invented.

sections.title: Capacity, execution milestones and runway
sections.text:
The Majivali project increases total combined capacity from 1.284 millionkg to 2.16 millionkg, a 68.22% uplift, not an additional 2.16 millionkg. Planned project cost is ₹21.7216 crore: land.9, civil 9.44, machinery 10.3472 and contingency 1.0344. Funding is IPO 14.6348 and internal 7.0868, including land paid on 13 March 2025.

Original milestones were civil work September–December 2025, machine delivery January 2026, installation/trials February and commercial production March 2026. The signed 31 March 2026 use certificate reports only ₹3.7211 crore capex use,25.43% of IPO capex allocation, with ₹10.9137 crore still earmarked. No verified commissioning evidence was found by cutoff. This does not prove abandonment or rule out additional internally funded deployment.

Conservative remaining project cost is ₹17.1005 crore, deducting only verified land and IPO-funded use. Additional certified internal expenditure would reduce it. Base completion 24 months from 31 March 2026, bear 30 months with 25% overrun and bull 18 months are analyst scenarios. Terminal base revenue ₹54.03 crore and bull ₹66.29 crore imply 78.17%/95.91% utilization of 2.16 millionkg at assumed ₹320/kg. That unit realization is a modeling proxy, not reported FY2026 actuals; adverse mix or prices would require more volume/capacity or lower sales.

sections.title: Dated funding and obligations
sections.text:
Opening 31 March 2026 cash ₹14.3305 crore is not entirely free: unused IPO funds ₹11.0333 crore comprise capex earmark 10.9137 and general-purpose earmark.1196. A ₹1.5 crore FD secures ₹1.3058 crore overdraft. The model settles that overdraft from unrestricted balances and releases the already-counted FD without adding it twice.

Vehicle term debt ₹.6559 crore at 7.6% is amortized with an analyst straight-principal five-year approximation, not the undisclosed exact 60-instalment schedule beginning 10 April 2026. MF/PMS carrying value ₹9.4725 crore is converted at 85% base/65% bear/95% bull. Sale before modeled April operating flows is an explicit assumption, not a claimed subsequent event. ICD principal ₹3 crore has unverified maturity/credit, so none funds operations; separate terminal recoveries are 50%/0%/80%.

Existing tax ₹.347 crore, statutory dues ₹.0477 crore, current gratuity ₹.1368 crore and GST reserve ₹.0413 crore are paid/reserved up front. TDS arrears are not added again on top of statutory balances. Long-term gratuity ₹.4133 crore is deducted once at terminal. Operating rent remains in margins; no Ind AS lease debt is invented.

Monthly cash checkpoints run from 31 March 2026 through 20 October 2026 entry to 20 October 2031 exit. Each interval is prefunded before receipts, and operating cash reserve is the greater of ₹.75 crore or 2.5% of current revenue run-rate. Working-capital absorption, earmarks, project spending and debt payments are each counted once. The modeled pre-entry April–October cash is not observed cash. Base is funded; linked bear stress breaches its floor, so no ordinary non-rescue return is reported.

At 31 March 2026 mutual-fund cost was about₹6.1051 crore against disclosed market value₹5.7427 crore, while the₹3.3673 crore PMS market value was not separately given. The model therefore does not assume carrying value equals immediately realizable cash. The ICD note names Dynamic Superways and Exports, Kent International and Maneckji Global, with balances including accrued interest of₹2.0570 crore,₹.0237 crore and₹1.0027 crore. Their contractual maturity and independent credit support were not established; none of these balances funds the operating model.

sections.title: Peer economics and valuation context
sections.text:
The relevant public comparisons are Plastiblends India, Polylink Polymers and Deep Polymers, not similarly named telecom/electronics companies. Plastiblends FY2026 sales ₹788.658 crore, operating EBITDA ₹66.0518 crore/margin 8.38% and PAT ₹36.6883 crore come from a much larger manufacturing/distribution system and broader mix. Polylink FY2026 sales ₹84.5964 crore and PAT ₹1.2234 crore declined 7.27% and 42.62%; current report FY2025 sales ₹91.2333 crore supersedes the older IPO peer snapshot ₹90.3209 crore.

Deep Polymers’ FY2025 prospectus snapshot gives sales ₹98.1716 crore, PAT ₹5.1992 crore and EBITDA margin 13.84%; it is explicitly not a FY2026/current-valuation comparison. Mehul’s FY2026 core margin 19.83% remains higher, but size, product mix and peak prior-year spreads can explain the difference without proving a moat.

No peer equity quotes were authenticated for the cutoff, so relative P/E or EV/EBITDA ranking is NS. Terminal EBIT multiples 7/10/12 are analyst assumptions, not invented peer medians. At the scenario price ₹49.61, normalized core NOPAT per current share≈₹4.0139 implies 12.36 times, versus about 10.02 times reported current-share earnings ₹4.95. These diagnostic multiples are not an executable-price recommendation.

sections.title: Conditional valuation, sensitivity and multibagger feasibility
sections.text:
The linked model uses an assumed ₹49.61 entry on 20 October 2026 and exit on 20 October 2031:1826 days/365.25, just under five years. Ordinary IRRs and IAS remain unavailable because price authentication and G2 are unresolved. Base and bull are fully funded under their assumptions; exact conditional returns and cash paths are displayed in the model summary below. Bear violates the prefunded reserve, so its diagnostic terminal price is not a valid ordinary non-rescue return.

Explicit rescue bear issues whole new shares at 60% of ₹49.61 with 5% fees, before each liquidity breach. Gross funding, shares, ownership dilution and rescued return are linked. Rescue hurdle entry-price outputs are null because changing entry price changes the required share issuance; a fixed-price dilution schedule cannot be reused as a solved buy price.

The genuine two-way tests cover ONWC 30/34/40/46% against project cost 80/100/125/150%, and EBIT margins 14/18.5/22% against exit multiples 7/10/13. Additional linked tests cover treasury realization, operating reserve and transaction costs. The 15% reverse-expectations calculation searches a finite funded bracket, checks residual error and discloses the implied constant revenue-growth solution near 5.95%. It remains conditional on margins, capital needs and exit multiple, not a statement of what an authenticated market price demands.

A 5× or 10× share price from ₹49.61 means ₹248.05 or ₹496.10 and roughly 38.0% or 58.5% annual returns over five years, before friction. At the base 10× EBIT multiple and 18.5% margin, even retaining base terminal surplus assets, these prices require roughly ₹127 crore/₹268 crore revenue. Existing planned capacity at the assumed ₹320/kg supports only ₹69.12 crore at 100% utilization. Thus 5×/10× requires another major expansion, materially higher realization/margin, a much larger multiple, or some combination with new funding. Neither outcome follows from the currently funded project; no multibagger probability is assigned.

Date convention:20October2026 is the Dussehra exchange holiday. It is the analytical valuation/horizon origin, not a claimed executed purchase date. The previous-session19October quote remains unverified for Mehul Colours; no trade is assumed to occur on the holiday. The requested20October2026 to20October2031 valuation horizon is preserved.

sections.title: SME execution and exact score audit
sections.text:
The official 19 October interoperability master establishes ISIN, share count and a 1,600-share lot. It does not establish an NSE listing, executable BSE price or realized turnover. At the scenario ₹49.61, one lot costs ₹79,376. A ₹5 lakh budget permits 6 lots/9,600 shares costing ₹476,256;7 lots/11,200 shares would cost ₹555,632.

Public float 28.35% and 345 holders do not establish liquidity. No verified 20/60-session traded value/volume, zero-turnover days, circuit frequency, bid–ask depth or 2/5/10% participation capacity was retrieved. A denied BSE archive response is HTML, not a zero-volume observation. L is NS and G4 is Hold-unresolved, not a claim that the stock cannot trade.

Primitive scores are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 6, EXEC 5, EARN 4; R, D, P, L are NS. BQS exact 4.90 and GQS exact 5.15 display 4.9 and 5.2 using Decimal half-up rounding. IAS uses unrounded BQS as Q, giving known contribution 1.225 with 25% coverage and possible range 1.975–8.725; this range is not a point estimate. All factors include two facts, contrary evidence, confidence and source references. G2 independently removes quality/growth/investment ranking eligibility. No midpoint imputation, small-company bonus or valuation override is used.

Judgment sensitivity: moving uncertain REV and CAP together by minus/plus one point, with every other factor fixed, gives BQS4.66–5.14 and GQS4.60–5.70. Changing REV alone gives BQS4.78–5.02/GQS4.75–5.55; CAP alone gives BQS4.78–5.02/GQS5.00–5.30. These are judgment scenarios, not confidence intervals or a reranking. IAS remainsNS and all ranking exclusions remain binding.

sections.title: Monitoring dashboard and change-of-view conditions
sections.text:
Monitoring thresholds below are analytical triggers, not management guidance. Review on each half-year result and project update; do not infer a change from silence alone.

1. Reporting reliability: baseline contradictory CARO clauses. Warning: no signed correction with the next statutory filing. Thesis break: confirmed material misstatement, scope restriction or unexplained diversion of IPO funds.
2. Core EBITDA margin: FY2026 baseline 19.83%. Warning below 17% for a half-year; thesis break below 14% for two comparable halves without a credible price/volume recovery bridge.
3. Receivable days: closing baseline 95.54 days. Warning above 110; thesis break above 130 plus worsening aged balances, rather than a seasonal date alone.
4. Good receivables over six months: baseline ₹.3143 crore/3.95% of net receivables. Warning above 8%; thesis break above 12% with no collections or adequate provisions.
5. Adjusted operating CFO/PAT: three-year baseline 48.26%. Improvement requires at least 80% across two years; warning below 50% over the next two halves after capital-advance normalization; thesis break sustained negative operating cash despite profits.
6. Project delivery: baseline 25.43% of IPO capex allocation used at 31 March 2026, commercial start not verified. Warning: no independently evidenced revised schedule/cost-to-complete. Thesis break: remaining cost cannot be funded while protecting earmarks and operating reserve.
7. Incremental returns: baseline 10.40% against 12–15% capital cost. Improvement requires post-commissioning returns above 15% on identifiable capital; thesis break below 10% after a reasonable two-year ramp with no corrective plan.
8. Treasury/ICDs: baseline ₹9.4725 crore financial investments plus ₹3 crore ICD principal. Warning any missed contractual collection, undisclosed relatedness or restriction; thesis break material unrecoverability that creates a funded-project cash deficit.
9. Customer concentration: baseline top 10 sales 48.19%. Warning above 60% or a top customer loss; thesis break contribution loss and unreplaced volume that invalidate the base margin/funding path.
10. Executability: baseline unknown 20/60-session trading capacity. Do not initiate an assessed position until an authenticated quote and lot-rounded participation/exit test support its size. A new positive quote alone does not clear G4.

Resolve EPS denominator, gratuity roll-forward and cashflow classification alongside the main audit corrections. Improve the business view only when incremental profitable growth produces cash without adverse dilution and the commissioned project earns above its capital cost. Keep ordinary operating risks separate from missing evidence; neither missing data nor a clean opinion should predetermine the outcome.
